patient_information: A 3-year-old boy from a rural area in Laos who is developing normally and is up to date with vaccinations. He had no history of previous ear infections or dental problems and had been previously well.
chief_complaint: A 10-day history of gradual, painful swelling of the right cheek with associated fever and poor appetite.
history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 10-day history of a gradual, painful swelling of the right cheek, accompanied by fever and poor appetite. Three days prior to presentation, his mother noticed a purulent discharge from his right ear. He had no cough, vomiting, or diarrhea, and no known history of trauma.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient is from rural Laos, an area endemic for melioidosis. His parents are rice farmers, and it was considered likely that the boy was frequently exposed to soil and water containing B. pseudomallei in the paddy fields.
vitals: The patient had a fever of 39.5°C (103.1°F).
physical_exam: The child appeared unwell. Examination revealed a localized, fluctuant, hot, and tender swelling of 6 to 8 cm in diameter below and anterior to the right ear, consistent with a parotid mass. A purulent discharge was present in the right auditory canal, with a suspected fistula from which the pus was arising. A right lower motor neuron facial nerve palsy was noted. The oral cavity and throat were unremarkable. There was no lymphadenopathy or hepatosplenomegaly, and cardiac and pulmonary exams were normal.
labs_and_diagnostics: Laboratory results showed a white blood cell count of 16.5 x10^9/L with 90% neutrophils and anemia with a hemoglobin of 9.4 g/dL. Pus cultures from both the right ear and the parotid abscess isolated Burkholderia pseudomallei. A blood culture was negative. Chest radiography and abdominal ultrasound were normal.
differential_diagnosis: The differential diagnosis for acute, suppurative, unilateral parotitis included common bacterial pathogens like Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes. Given the endemic location in Laos, Burkholderia pseudomallei causing melioidosis was a primary consideration. Mumps was considered less likely because the swelling was suppurative and unilateral, whereas mumps parotitis is typically non-suppurative and becomes bilateral. Other viral causes and chronic granulomatous parotitis were also less likely given the acute and highly inflammatory presentation.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient underwent incision and drainage of the parotid abscess, which yielded copious pus. He was treated with intravenous ceftazidime for 10 days, followed by a 16-week course of oral co-amoxiclav. He had a good clinical response, no complications occurred, and no underlying predisposing disease was identified.
final_diagnosis: The final diagnosis was suppurative parotitis due to melioidosis. This was confirmed by the isolation of the causative agent, Burkholderia pseudomallei, from cultures of pus from both the ear discharge and the drained parotid abscess. The patient's clinical presentation was classic for pediatric melioidosis in an endemic region like Laos, where it is a common cause of this condition.
